hints: nums is sorted, so all copies of a value sit next to each other. How can you tell that an element is the first of its group?
Write-pointer technique: an element is new exactly when it differs from the last value you kept. Copy it to position k, advance k, and at the end return the first k elements.

1. Keep nums[0]; set k = 1.
  2. For i from 1 to n−1: if nums[i] != nums[k-1], set nums[k] = nums[i], k++.
  3. Return a copy of nums[0..k-1].

approaches.name: Brute force
approaches.idea: Put every value into a set and then sort the set's contents.

approaches.name: Optimal
approaches.idea: Because equal values are adjacent, compare each element with the last kept one and copy forward with a write pointer.

explain: For nums = [1, 1, 2, 3, 3, 3, 5]: 1 is kept; the second 1 equals the last kept value and is skipped; 2, 3 and 5 each differ from the last kept value, so they are copied forward, giving k = 4 and the result [1, 2, 3, 5]. The invariant is that nums[0..k-1] holds each distinct value once, in order. A single-element array simply returns that one value.
recognize: "Sorted array + remove duplicates in place" → compare with the last kept value, write pointer.
javascript: function removeDuplicates(nums) { const out = []; for (const x of nums) if (!out.length || out[out.length - 1] !== x) out.push(x); return out; }
